title: Vector-store episodic memory
description: Agents store past observations as embeddings in a vector database (FAISS, Chroma, Pinecone). At each step, the agent retrieves the k most similar past episodes and injects them into context — recall by semantic similarity instead of recency, so relevant history from weeks ago surfaces when it matters.
method: Embed observations (sentence transformers); upsert with metadata (timestamp, session, salience); query top-k by cosine similarity with recency/salience re-ranking.
usage: Write salient events only (not every step); tag with session and timestamp; tune k and the re-ranker for your task.

demo.code:
mem = [('user likes tea', 0.9), ('deploy failed tuesday', 0.7)]
q = 'beverage'
hits = sorted(mem, key=lambda m: (q in m[0], m[1]), reverse=True)
print('recall for', repr(q), '->', hits[0][0])

title: Knowledge-graph entity memory
description: Instead of raw text, the agent maintains a knowledge graph of entities and relations (user -works_at-> Acme; Acme -deploys-> Friday). Graph memory supports multi-hop recall ('who works on the Friday deploy?') that flat text search can't, and updates are surgical (change one edge, not a whole summary).
method: Extract (subject, relation, object) triples from observations; upsert into the graph; answer recall queries by graph traversal with embedding fallback.
usage: Define the relation schema for your domain; extract triples on write; traverse on recall.

title: Working-memory scratchpad with tools
description: The scratchpad is the agent's desk: a structured working area (current goal, hypotheses, plan steps, open questions) rewritten each turn, separate from the raw transcript. It keeps long tasks coherent by making the agent's current mental state explicit and inspectable instead of buried in chat history.
method: Maintain a scratchpad object (goal, plan[], hypotheses, blockers); the model updates it each turn via a structured call; tools read/write designated sections.
usage: Keep the scratchpad small and current; archive completed plans to episodic memory; never let it grow unbounded.

demo.code:
pad = {'goal': 'fix deploy', 'plan': ['read logs', 'patch config'], 'blockers': []}
print('scratchpad:', pad)
pad['plan'].append('redeploy')
print('updated plan:', pad['plan'])

title: Episodic timeline with temporal queries
description: Episodic memory keeps a timestamped timeline of what happened, enabling 'what did we decide last Tuesday?' queries. Temporal indexing (by session, day, project phase) plus natural-language time resolution turns the agent's past into a queryable log instead of a fading blur.
method: Index episodes by timestamp and session; resolve time expressions ('last Tuesday', 'during the deploy') to ranges; retrieve episodes in range, ranked by relevance.
usage: Always timestamp writes; resolve relative times against the session clock; show dates in recall answers.

demo.code:
episodes = [('2026-10-18', 'decided to use Postgres'), ('2026-10-19', 'deploy failed')]
q = [e for d, e in episodes if d == '2026-10-18']
print('what did we decide on 2026-10-18?', q)

title: Memory consolidation during idle
description: Like sleep for brains: when the agent is idle, a background process replays recent episodes, merges duplicates, extracts durable facts, and prunes noise. Consolidation turns a pile of raw episodes into a clean, queryable long-term store without spending foreground tokens.
method: Idle trigger -> replay recent episodes -> deduplicate -> extract facts to semantic store -> prune raw episodes -> update indexes.
usage: Run consolidation on a schedule; keep raw episodes for a retention window in case consolidation errs.

demo.code:
episodes = ['user likes tea', 'user likes tea (again)', 'deploy at 3pm']
unique = list(dict.fromkeys(episodes))
print('consolidated', len(episodes), '->', len(unique), 'episodes; facts extracted to semantic store')

title: Cross-agent shared memory bus
description: In multi-agent systems, a shared memory bus lets agents publish findings and subscribe to topics instead of passing everything through messages. One agent's discovered fact becomes everyone's recallable memory, with provenance tracking so consumers know who learned what.
method: Publish/subscribe topics on a shared store; writes carry agent id and timestamp; subscribers get notified; provenance rides on every entry.
usage: Namespace topics per task; set write permissions per agent role; expire transient findings.

title: Salience-scored memory writes
description: Writing everything to long-term memory drowns signal in noise. Salience scoring has the agent rate each observation's future usefulness (user preferences: high; transient tool output: low) and only persists above-threshold items, keeping the memory store dense with things worth remembering.
method: Score each candidate write 0-1 on predicted future utility; persist above threshold; decay scores over time so stale facts fade unless reinforced.
usage: Calibrate the threshold on real sessions: too high loses preferences, too low floods the store.

demo.code:
cands = [('user name is Manon', 0.95), ('temp file listed', 0.1)]
kept = [c for c, s in cands if s >= 0.5]
print('persisted:', kept, '| dropped: temp file listed')

title: SQLite session journal
description: The humble durable option: every agent step appends to a local SQLite journal (timestamp, action, observation, tokens). Sessions resume by replaying the journal; analytics query it with SQL; nothing depends on a vector DB being up. Simple, inspectable, and effectively free.
method: Append-only events table; session id per run; resume replays events into context; SQL for analytics and debugging.
usage: Journal everything; build resume and analytics on top; add vector search later if recall quality demands it.

demo.code:
import sqlite3
c = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
c.execute('CREATE TABLE events(ts TEXT, kind TEXT, payload TEXT)')
c.execute("INSERT INTO events VALUES ('10:01','note','user likes tea')")
print('journal rows:', c.execute('SELECT * FROM events').fetchall())
